bugs.error_message: PR #164 CI failed: cargo-deny 'error[vulnerability]: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries' (RUSTSEC-2026-0285) and Security Vulnerability Scan (cargo audit) exit 1 on the same advisory
bugs.root_cause: Cargo.lock pinned rustls v0.23.44 (transitive: kube client -> hyper-rustls -> rustls), which is below the RUSTSEC-2026-0285 / GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc fix version 0.23.45
bugs.fix: cargo update -p rustls (0.23.44 -> 0.23.45, lockfile-only); verified with `cargo deny check advisories` -> ok; changelog entry added

bugs.error_message: Dependabot PRs #173/#174 failed all CodeQL jobs: "Loaded a configuration file for version '4.38.1', but running version '4.38.0'"
bugs.root_cause: codeql-action monorepo sub-actions (init/analyze/upload-sarif) are distinct dependency names; the dependabot.yml group pattern 'github/codeql-action' matched none of them, so the family split into three PRs and any single bump mismatches init vs analyze
bugs.fix: re-pinned all six github/codeql-action/* refs to v4.38.1 (1c5b675) in one change across codeql/sast/scorecard/build workflows; added 'github/codeql-action/*' to the actions-routine group so the family bumps as one PR

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job: setup_file failed at `out=$(patch_annotation ...)` right after the admission policy applied; 'bats warning: Executed 1 instead of expected 5 tests'
bugs.root_cause: bats executes setup_file with errexit; the activation poll's probe patch exits non-zero exactly when the policy starts denying (the success condition), so the awaited denial aborted the file at the assignment
bugs.fix: append `|| true` to the probe assignment (comment marks it load-bearing); all other patch_annotation call sites already use bats `run`

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job round five: setup passes, then tests 1/2 fail the message assertion and tests 4/5 fail their allow assertion; only test 3 passes
bugs.root_cause: patch_annotation interpolated the value into the patch JSON unescaped; JSON-shaped values like {"namespace":"x"} broke the patch document, so kubectl exited non-zero with a PARSE error before any request — deny tests saw the wrong message, allow tests saw a failure; quote-free values (probe-N, deadbeef) worked, masking it in setup and test 3
bugs.fix: escape embedded quotes in the value (${value//\"/\\\"}) before building the -p document; verified unescaped form fails json.load and escaped form round-trips

bugs.error_message: ScheduledCapacity controller re-patched its own status on every reconcile, re-triggering its own watch: ~50 resourceVersion bumps/sec and a single handback timeout counted 100 times in the Prometheus counter.
bugs.root_cause: Three compounding mistakes in patch_status. (1) Condition::new() stamps lastTransitionTime with Utc::now(), so the computed condition set never equalled the stored one and every reconcile wrote. (2) There was no no-op guard comparing the computed status against the stored one before patching. (3) record_decision_metrics incremented the handback-timeout counter once per reconcile instead of once per transition into the phase. A later rewrite then introduced a fourth: build_status_value silently dropped the targetRef and spotSchedule keys, so the new no-op guard compared a desired status that could never equal the stored one and was permanently disabled, with no test failure and no visible symptom.
bugs.fix: merge_condition_timestamps() preserves each condition's lastTransitionTime unless its `status` actually changed (matched by type, not position); spot_schedule_transition_time() does the same for the mirrored provider timestamp. patch_status() deserialises the computed status into ScheduledCapacityStatus and returns early when it equals the stored one. record_decision_metrics() gates on entered_phase(). build_status_value() always emits every key the controller owns, using explicit JSON null for cleared fields (an omitted key in a merge patch leaves the stored value, so handbackDeadline could never be cleared). Guarded by test_build_status_value_emits_every_field_of_the_status_type, which derives the expected key set from a fully-populated ScheduledCapacityStatus rather than a hand-written list.
bugs.lesson: A controller that logs nothing on a successful reconcile cannot be debugged: the missing-success-log made a working watch look dead and sent the first diagnosis in the wrong direction. Always log reconcile completion. And any status field built by hand must be checked against the type, not against memory.

bugs.error_message: Machine create rejected by Cluster API v1.14.3: 'Machine in version "v1beta2" cannot be handled as a Machine: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.bootstrap.configRef.apiVersion", unknown field "spec.bootstrap.configRef.namespace", unknown field "spec.infrastructureRef.apiVersion", unknown field "spec.infrastructureRef.namespace"'
bugs.root_cause: Only half of the CAPI version-agnostic design was implemented. resolve_capi_machine_version() discovered the served Machine version correctly (v1beta2 on CAPI v1.11+), but add_machine_to_cluster built spec.bootstrap.configRef and spec.infrastructureRef in exactly one shape: the v1beta1 core ObjectReference with apiVersion + namespace. v1beta2 replaced both with a ContractVersionedObjectReference whose only fields are apiGroup, kind and name, and the Machine type decodes strictly, so the surplus fields are a hard BadRequest rather than being pruned. It survived review because machine_api_version_for() passes the user's bootstrapSpec version through, so a ScheduledMachine declaring bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 produced a self-consistent v1beta1 Machine that the conversion webhook accepted; only a v1beta2 spec or the discovery fallback reached the bug, and every unit fixture assumes v1beta1.
bugs.fix: machine_contract_ref() in src/reconcilers/helpers.rs is now the only place either shape is written, keyed on uses_legacy_object_reference() against CAPI_LEGACY_OBJECT_REFERENCE_VERSIONS (v1alpha3, v1alpha4, v1beta1) in src/constants.rs. An unrecognised version resolves to the MODERN shape, since the legacy one is being removed. Six tests in helpers_tests.rs pin both shapes, the group derivation (version segment dropped) and the unknown-version default. ADR 0017. Verified live: Machine stored at cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2 with apiGroup-form refs, phase Running, Node Ready.
bugs.lesson: Discovering a version is not the same as honouring its contract. When a controller branches on a discovered API version, every field whose SHAPE changed with that version has to branch too, and a unit suite whose fixtures all pin the old version cannot tell you otherwise. A passthrough default (here: the user's bootstrapSpec version) can keep the common path self-consistent and hide the bug on exactly the path that is the future.

bugs.error_message: Controller's Machine and Node secondary watches matched nothing: watch issued with labelSelector=5spot.eribourg.dev%2Fscheduled-machine while every created Machine was stamped 5spot.finos.org/scheduled-machine. Machine/Node state changes never triggered a reconcile of the owning ScheduledMachine.
bugs.root_cause: The API group rename from 5spot.eribourg.dev to 5spot.finos.org never reached src/labels.rs. Two constants described the same key: constants::SCHEDULED_MACHINE_LABEL (finos), which merge_owned_labels() STAMPS on every Machine, bootstrap and infra resource, and labels::LABEL_SCHEDULED_MACHINE (eribourg), which main.rs SELECTS on for both secondary watches and which machine_to_scheduled_machine()/node_to_scheduled_machines_via_machine() read. Security consequence: RESERVED_LABEL_PREFIXES covers 5spot.finos.org/ but not the retired domain, so the one key the reverse mapping trusted was injectable through machineTemplate.labels. An existing test had enshrined the bug, asserting that the canonical 5spot.finos.org key was an 'imposter'.
bugs.fix: labels::LABEL_SCHEDULED_MACHINE is now an alias of constants::SCHEDULED_MACHINE_LABEL, so the stamped key and the watched key are one definition and cannot drift; the five other 5-Spot label constants move to 5spot.finos.org. Three drift guards in labels_tests.rs (alias holds, no key on the retired group, owned key covered by RESERVED_LABEL_PREFIXES). test_machine_to_sm_wrong_prefix_label_is_ignored rewritten to use genuinely foreign prefixes and to assert the retired group no longer resolves. Threat model 1.7: T2's mitigation marked incomplete for that period, new T12 for tracking-label confusion.
bugs.lesson: Two string literals for one key will drift, and a label used on BOTH the write and the read side is the worst place for it: nothing fails, the watch just silently matches nothing, so the controller degrades from event-driven to timer-driven with no error anywhere. Alias the one constant instead of repeating the string. Also: a test asserting that the CORRECT value is wrong is the loudest possible signal that a rename was left half-finished, so when a test calls something an imposter, check which side is actually canonical.
